diagnoses.label: Export/ingress leak-only fixes miscategorized as oscillation fixes
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill's Tier 2 export-policy guidance conflates leak-only mitigations (no-export community, block provider→peer export, ingress AS_PATH filtering, RPKI) with oscillation resolution. It states filtering peer-learned routes before re-advertising breaks the cycle, but does not distinguish this from filtering provider→peer exports, which stops the leak without removing the mutual peer-learned preference edges that create the cycle. As a result, the agent labels no-export/ingress/RPKI-style solutions as resolving oscillation too.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Verifier failed 4 solutions where the agent marked oscillation_resolved=True but expected False: 'Configure export policy on vhubvnet1 ... to block announcing provider routes ... to peer vhubvnet2', 'Enable ingress filtering on vhubvnet2 ... reject routes with AS_PATH containing 65001', 'Enable RPKI origin validation ...', and 'Configure route policy on vhubvnet1 to enforce no-export of provider routes to peer vhubvnet2 by bgp community'. Agent's summary explicitly justified these as breaking the preference cycle by citing the skill's Tier 2 guidance.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A decision rule that separates (a) fixes that remove the mutual peer-learned edges causing the preference cycle (which resolve oscillation) from (b) fixes that only block provider-learned or leaked routes from being exported/accepted (which resolve leaks but leave the peer-preference cycle intact). The skill also fails to state that RPKI origin validation does not address a valley-free export leak whose origin is legitimate.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In the fix-selection section, add explicit criteria: oscillation is resolved only when the preference cycle edges themselves are removed or overridden (e.g., preference change, forwarding-plane override, filtering the specific peer-learned routes that feed the cycle). Leak-only mitigations (no-export community on a subset of routes, export block of provider routes to peer, ingress AS_PATH filter, RPKI) should be classified as resolving leaks but not oscillation unless they also eliminate the mutual preference edges. Include a checklist step that evaluates each candidate against both criteria independently and clarify RPKI's scope (origin authorization, not valley-free export).

diagnoses.label: Insufficient guidance for parallax-heavy scenes
diagnoses.general_pattern: The dyn-object-masks skill prescribes a single approach (2D affine/homography warp + intensity differencing + adaptive threshold + morphology) without warning that this approach fails on scenes with strong translational camera motion (walking/dolly) where parallax residuals dominate. It offers no alternative or decision criterion for switching methods, so the agent either produces massive false-positive masks (~15-20% of image) or, after ad-hoc switching to flow-residual methods, over-suppresses to near-empty masks.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Run produced Mean IoU 0.0143 and Boundary IoU 0.0008. Initial affine-differencing yielded ~15-20% pixel nnz per frame (verifier log lines 'mask frame k: nnz=~130k-190k (14-21%)'). Agent then switched to flow-residual method producing mostly 0-nnz frames (frames 10-17 all nnz=0). No skill guidance addressed either failure mode.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The skill lacks a step to (a) diagnose whether a 2D global motion model is adequate (e.g., via residual distribution, dolly-in / large translation detection) and (b) select or combine a flow-consistency-based alternative when parallax is significant, plus sanity checks on plausible foreground fraction.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add explicit guidance: when egomotion indicates translational/dolly motion or when residual statistics show heavy tails covering large image fractions, switch from intensity differencing to a flow-direction/consistency check (residual optical flow against a fitted global flow model with epipolar or motion-consistency reasoning), and set a plausibility band on foreground area to reject implausible outputs.

diagnoses.label: Missing threshold/area calibration guidance for mask size plausibility
diagnoses.general_pattern: The dyn-object-masks skill provides only illustrative constants (min threshold 20, area floor) with no rule for validating that final mask coverage is plausible. There is no self-check that flags frames where the moving-object fraction is implausibly high (e.g., >~10% of image) or entirely empty in scenes known to contain moving objects, so silent failures pass the local checks.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Multiple pipelines were tried; final masks ranged from 0% to 9% nnz per frame with no automated re-tuning. Verifier reports Mean IoU 0.0143 and P10 IoU 0.0000, indicating masks bear little spatial relation to ground truth despite passing format checks.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A plausibility self-check on per-frame foreground fraction and temporal consistency, plus a directive to re-tune threshold/area when fraction is out of expected band.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add self-check items: expected foreground fraction bounds, temporal continuity of connected components, and a documented calibration loop to adjust threshold multiplier and min-area when outputs fall outside plausible bands.

diagnoses.label: Output-validation skill omits mask-content plausibility checks
diagnoses.general_pattern: output-validation focuses on structural correctness (keys, shape, CSR integrity) but does not include any content-level sanity checks for mask outputs (e.g., non-trivial coverage, temporal smoothness, foreground area range). Structural validity therefore hides content failure.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Agent's validation step reported 'Instructions VALID' and 'NPZ VALID' while final masks scored Mean IoU 0.0143; verifier's format tests all passed and only test_mask_comprehensive failed.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A content-level validation step for masks (coverage bounds per frame, flicker/temporal consistency, non-empty across frames when motion labels are non-Stay) as part of the pre-submission checklist.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Extend output-validation with mask-content sanity checks (plausible foreground fraction band, temporal flicker bound, correlation between non-Stay motion intervals and mask activity) so that structural passes do not mask semantic failures.

package_assessment.rationale: Motion labeling passed (Macro-F1 0.86) and all format checks passed; the sole failure is mask quality (Mean IoU 0.014). Both the dyn-object-masks skill (single-model approach, no parallax handling, weak calibration/self-check guidance) and output-validation skill (no content-level mask sanity checks) contain reusable deficiencies that plausibly caused the failure without invoking task-specific answers.

diagnoses.label: Reviewer enumeration under-recall across evidence channels
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill's reviewer extraction guidance stops at a single evidence channel (one review meeting's participants who spoke). It does not require the agent to union reviewer signals across ALL evidence channels — document `feedback` sections, PR reviewer fields, slack thread replies to the report-share message, and multiple related meeting transcripts — before returning the final set. As a result, when reviewers are distributed across multiple artifacts, the agent stops after the first artifact yields a plausible list and under-reports the count.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: For q1 the agent returned 8 IDs derived solely from participants of a single meeting (`CoFoAIX_planning_1`) who spoke in the transcript. Verifier reports `q1 length mismatch. Expected 11, got 8`. The trajectory shows the agent inspected document `feedback` text (present on documents 1 and 2) but never extracted attributed reviewers from those feedback sections, nor from slack thread replies to the report-share message, nor from PR reviewer fields, before finalizing.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: An explicit 'union across evidence channels' step: after collecting Tier 1/2/3 reviewer candidates from each channel (explicit reviewer fields, document feedback attributions, meeting transcript contributors, slack thread replies to the report-share message, PR reviewers), merge and de-duplicate them, and only stop when all channels tied to the selected report have been exhausted.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Restructure Step 5 to require the agent to (a) enumerate every artifact linked to the chosen report (document, slack share thread + replies, all meetings whose transcripts/chats discuss the report, PRs introducing it), (b) apply the reviewer tier rules to each artifact independently, (c) union the resulting employee IDs, and (d) record which channel contributed each ID before returning. Add a completeness checklist that fails 'USE_EVIDENCE' if any linked artifact was not searched for reviewer contributions.
diagnoses.target_section: Step 5 — Extract key reviewers (DO NOT equate "participants" with reviewers)

diagnoses.label: No completeness/self-check gate before returning reviewer set

Without such a gate, the agent commits to the first coherent list it assembles, even when other clearly relevant artifacts (e.g., document `feedback` fields it already read) have not been mined for attributions.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: The agent read documents whose `feedback` fields contained explicit suggestions (docs 1 and 2 in CoachForce.json) but never mapped those feedback bullets to contributor IDs, and finalized the answer immediately after one meeting-transcript pass. No re-check step was triggered despite the skill's own NEED_MORE_SEARCH recommendation type existing.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add an explicit pre-output checklist and downgrade the recommendation to NEED_MORE_SEARCH whenever any linked artifact carrying potential reviewer contributions has not been individually inspected and attributed.

diagnoses.label: no build-fix skill for CI/tox failures
diagnoses.general_pattern: The provided skill bundle contains no guidance for diagnosing or repairing Python build/CI failures (tox environments, missing optional dependencies, flaky/time-based test assertions, pyproject.toml/tox.ini alignment). The four preloaded skills cover CI log analysis, Temporal testing, pytest style, and uv usage—none map to the presented task of restoring a green tox-based build across multiple Python versions.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Preloaded skills are analyze-ci, temporal-python-testing, testing-python, uv-package-manager. Task requires fixing a tox build for AgentOps-AI. Verifier shows tox py37/38/39 missing interpreters and test_record_timestamp failing due to millisecond-precision timestamp collision (init_timestamp == end_timestamp). Agent addressed only the ImportError, explicitly declared the timestamp failure 'out of scope,' and finished; verifier reports Build failed in the passed job.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A decision procedure that (a) requires reproducing the exact CI harness (tox across the declared envlist) before declaring success, (b) treats every failing test surfaced by the harness as in-scope for a build-fix task, and (c) prompts inspection of test-versus-source timing/precision mismatches and interpreter-availability constraints in tox envlist.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a skill that frames 'fix-build' tasks as: reproduce the CI command exactly, enumerate all failing signals (collection errors, interpreter selection, per-test failures), classify each as configuration vs. code, and only stop when the CI command exits zero. Include heuristics for narrowing the tox envlist to available interpreters and for handling sub-second timestamp precision issues in helper utilities.
diagnoses.target_section: Running Tests / Checklist (or a new 'Diagnosing failing builds' section)

diagnoses.label: premature-success heuristic
diagnoses.general_pattern: None of the skills instruct the agent to keep iterating until the authoritative build command passes; the agent is free to label remaining failures 'pre-existing/unrelated' and finish. This yields false-positive completions on build-repair tasks whose success criterion is exit-zero of the CI script.

Verifier ran run_passed.sh (tox) and failed with the same test_record_timestamp assertion across py310/py311/py312 plus missing interpreters for py37/38/39.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Explicit stop condition tying task completion to the exit status of the project's actual build/test entrypoint (e.g., run_passed.sh / tox) rather than the agent's judgment about which failures are relevant.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document a mandatory verification loop: identify the canonical build command, run it end-to-end, and treat any nonzero exit as unresolved—prohibit categorizing surfaced failures as out-of-scope without evidence that they existed and were tolerated in the original green build.

A skill package targeting fix-build tasks with explicit verification and scoping rules would have redirected the agent to keep investigating.

diagnoses.label: OCR post-processing lacks receipt total-extraction guidance
diagnoses.general_pattern: The image-ocr skill documents raw text extraction, multi-pass OCR, and preprocessing, but provides no reusable guidance for the downstream step of parsing structured fields (totals, dates) from noisy receipt OCR output. When Tesseract yields characters like colons or letters embedded in numbers (e.g., '92:80' instead of '92.80'), a naive numeric regex fails and returns null, even though the correct keyword line was located.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Verifier failed at row 16 col 3: actual '' vs expected '92.80'. Trajectory shows OCR for 078.jpg produced lines like 'a Total — 92:80' and 'GrandTotal. = SSCS 92.80'; the agent's NUM_RE required a '.' decimal separator and rejected '92:80'/'92 80' variants, so extract_total_candidates returned empty and the cell was left blank.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The skill never tells the caller to (a) normalize common OCR digit-adjacency artifacts (':' or spaces between the integer and decimal part, stray letters attached to numbers) before applying numeric regexes, or (b) cross-validate a keyword-line hit by scanning neighboring OCR variants when the primary variant fails to yield a clean number.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a 'Post-OCR numeric normalization' subsection to the image-ocr skill that warns Tesseract frequently substitutes ':' for '.', inserts spaces inside decimals, and glues letters to digits; recommend normalizing such patterns before regex extraction and combining candidates across multiple preprocessing/PSM passes rather than accepting the first variant's numeric parse.
diagnoses.target_section: Multi-Pass OCR Strategy / new 'Post-OCR Numeric Normalization' subsection

diagnoses.label: No guidance on task-length budgeting for batch OCR pipelines
diagnoses.general_pattern: The image-ocr skill's Batch Processing example iterates over a directory with a single OCR pass per file but gives no guidance on structuring an end-to-end pipeline (OCR + parse + write output) so it completes within a bounded iteration/turn budget. Callers naturally expand into multi-pass OCR plus iterative debugging, exhausting the agent budget before producing the required output file.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: The run terminated with stop_reason 'max_iterations' after 65 iterations while the agent was still tuning preprocessing variants for a single failing image (078.jpg). The verifier had to run against a stale xlsx that still contained a blank total, indicating the agent never converged on a completed extraction within the available turns.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: The skill lacks a 'Plan before iterating' step: decide on a fixed OCR variant set, run the full batch once, write the output artifact, and only then diagnose per-file failures with targeted re-OCR — instead of interleaving whole-batch reruns for every heuristic tweak.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add batch-workflow guidance recommending: (1) produce the required output artifact after the first full pass so partial results are always available, (2) cap the number of preprocessing/PSM variants tried per image, and (3) isolate per-image debugging to a subset rather than re-running the whole directory on every change.

package_assessment.rationale: The single verifier failure (blank total for 078.jpg where OCR clearly saw 'Grand Total ... 92.80'/'92:80') stems from missing image-ocr guidance on normalizing common Tesseract digit artifacts before numeric parsing, and the run-out of iterations reflects missing batch-workflow guidance. Both are reusable, skill-level deficiencies in image-ocr/SKILL.md rather than task-specific answers or infrastructure faults.

diagnoses.label: Incomplete equal-contribution footnote pattern coverage
diagnoses.general_pattern: Skill lists 'Equal contribution' as a pattern to redact but only shows two exact-string examples ('Equal contribution', '* Equal contribution'). It does not enumerate common typographic variants (e.g., asterisk without space, dagger/double-dagger markers, superscript symbols, 'These authors contributed equally', 'Co-first authors') nor instruct agents to search for the phrase 'equal contribution' case-insensitively / as a substring. Agents following the literal example may build a redaction list that misses variants actually present in papers.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Verifier failed test_identifiers_redacted with 'paper3.pdf: identifiers not redacted: ["Equal contribution"]'. Trajectory shows the extracted text contains '*Equal contribution' (asterisk directly adjacent, no space) on page 0 of paper3, and the agent's leak-check regex list did not include any 'equal contribution' pattern, so it was never added to the redaction list.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A required step to (a) always search for the case-insensitive substring 'equal contribution' (and common marker variants like *, †, ‡, superscripts) rather than a single exact string, and (b) verify post-redaction that no form of 'equal contribution' text remains before declaring success.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Expand the 'Equal contribution footnotes' guidance to require substring / case-insensitive detection of the phrase plus enumeration of typical marker prefixes, and add a verification check that scans redacted output for any remaining 'equal contribution' occurrence, treating any hit as a failure to fix.
diagnoses.target_section: Patterns to Redact (Before References Only) — item 8 'Equal contribution footnotes'

It does not verify that the categories of identifying information the skill itself enumerates (author names, affiliations, emails, arXiv IDs, DOIs, venues, equal-contribution notes) are actually absent from the redacted pre-references text. Agents therefore can pass 'verification' while leakage persists.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: The agent's own custom leak-scan (built ad hoc) did not include an 'equal contribution' pattern, and the skill-provided verify_redaction() would not have caught it either — it prints '✓ Verification passed' based only on length ratios. The run ended with the agent declaring success while an identifier still leaked, causing test_identifiers_redacted to fail.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A leak-audit step in verification that, for each pattern category listed in 'Patterns to Redact', re-scans the redacted document's pre-references pages and raises on any remaining match.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Extend the verification contract to include a per-category residual-leak check driven by the same pattern taxonomy the skill defines, so structural checks and content-leak checks are both mandatory before considering redaction complete.

package_assessment.rationale: The failure is a single leaked identifier ('Equal contribution' on paper3) that maps directly to two gaps in the academic-pdf-redaction skill: (1) the equal-contribution pattern guidance is under-specified and example-driven rather than substring/variant-driven, and (2) the mandated verification routine only checks length/structure and does not audit for residual identifier categories the skill itself enumerates. Both gaps are reusable, skill-controllable, and jointly explain why the agent believed the task was complete.

diagnoses.label: Ambiguous plan output format specification
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill's save-plan guidance says only 'standard PDDL plan format' and points to PDDLWriter, but never defines the concrete line syntax required for plan files. When the task prompt shows an example using functional syntax `action(arg1, arg2, ...)`, the skill does not warn that PDDL plan readers (e.g., unified_planning.PDDLReader.parse_plan) require Lisp-style `(action arg1 arg2 ...)` lines. Without this disambiguation, the agent formats each action using the misleading prompt example and produces plan files that a PDDL plan parser cannot interpret, even though the plan itself was validated in-memory.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: The agent wrote lines like `move_seg_rw_0_400_seg_rww_0_50_south_south_medium(airplane_cfbeg)`. The verifier's `reader.parse_plan(...)` raised `UPException: Cannot interpret move_seg_rw_0_400_seg_rww_0_50_south_south_medium(airplane_cfbeg)`, while the agent's own in-process `PlanValidator` reported `VALID`. The failure is purely a serialization/format mismatch, not a planning error.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A validation step that (a) specifies the exact required plan-file syntax (`(action arg1 arg2 ...)` per line, lowercase, no commas/parentheses around args) and (b) mandates round-tripping the written file back through `PDDLReader.parse_plan` before considering the task complete.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In the save-plan section, explicitly define the required per-line grammar for PDDL plan files, warn that prompt-provided illustrative examples may not match parser-accepted syntax, and prescribe using the library's own writer (or a documented template matching `parse_plan`'s regex) plus a post-write parse-back check to guarantee the file is machine-readable.

The skill provides no guidance to re-load and re-validate the written plan file.

diagnoses.label: Tokenizable modeled as subtype trait instead of type class
diagnoses.general_pattern: Skill guidance for translating Python `runtime_checkable` Protocol classes to Scala is missing. The idioms file shows Protocols/duck typing as 'no direct equivalent' and points to type classes generically, while the functional file only shows type classes for Show. Nothing explicitly maps `@runtime_checkable Protocol` to a Scala type class with implicit evidence, so the agent oscillated between a `Tokenizable[-A]` type class and a subtype `trait Tokenizable { def toToken: String }`, ultimately choosing subtype dispatch. This loses the structural/ad-hoc polymorphism the Python Protocol expressed and forces user types to extend the trait.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Trajectory shows the agent first defined `trait Tokenizable[-A] { def toToken(value: A): String }` with an implicit-based `tokenize[A](value: A)(implicit ev: Tokenizable[A])` overload, hit ambiguous-overload compile errors against `tokenize(value: Any)`, then reverted to `trait Tokenizable { def toToken: ***REDACTED*** }` and pattern-matched on it — the agent's own note comments 'mirroring Python's runtime_checkable Protocol' but abandoned the type-class approach because the skills gave no pattern for combining Any-dispatch with type-class dispatch.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A decision rule for translating `@runtime_checkable Protocol` (structural typing) to Scala: when to use a type class with implicit evidence vs. a subtype trait, and how to reconcile it with an `Any`-based runtime dispatcher (e.g., a `Tokenizable.instanceFor(Any): Option[String]` registry, or restricting the dispatcher to typed overloads).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add explicit guidance mapping Python Protocols to Scala type classes (with `implicit`/`given` evidence) as the default, note the alternative subtype-trait encoding, and warn that combining a type-class overload with an `Any` fallback causes overload ambiguity — suggesting workarounds (distinct method names, prioritized implicits, or a registry keyed by runtime class).

diagnoses.label: No guidance on Any-dispatch overloading pitfalls
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skills describe pattern matching on `Any` and type-class based generics separately, but never warn that mixing `def f(value: Any)` with `def f[A](value: A)(implicit ev: TC[A])` causes ambiguous-overload errors in Scala 2.13. Python's runtime `isinstance` dispatch commonly translates to both styles simultaneously, and the skill omits the interaction.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Compile errors: 'ambiguous reference to overloaded definition, both method tokenize ... of type [A](value: A)(implicit ev: Tokenizable[A]): Token and method tokenize ... of type (value: Any): Token match argument types (String) / (Int) / (LocalDate) / (Foo)'. The agent had to delete the type-class overload entirely to compile.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Explicit rule: when translating Python's dynamic dispatch (`isinstance` chains + Protocol matching) to Scala, pick a single dispatch mechanism per method name — either exhaustive pattern-match on `Any`, OR type-class overloads with distinct types — and if both are needed, use distinct method names or a Priority pattern.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document the overload-resolution pitfall and prescribe one of: (a) single `Any`-typed dispatcher that pattern-matches including a `case t: TokenizableTrait` branch; (b) type-class-only API with no `Any` overload; or (c) distinct method names (`tokenize` vs `tokenizeTC`) when both are required.

diagnoses.label: f-interpolator dynamic precision not documented
diagnoses.general_pattern: The syntax-mapping skill shows `f"Value: $x%.2f"` for fixed format specifiers but never explains that Scala's `f""` interpolator requires literal format strings — dynamic precision like `f"$d%.${precision}f"` does not compile. Python's f-string `f"{d:.{precision}f}"` supports embedded expressions in the spec, and the skill provides no equivalent guidance.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Compile errors on first attempt: 'Tokenizer.scala:177: error: Missing conversion operator in \'%\'; use %% for literal %, %n for newline — case d: Double => f"$d%.${precision}f"' and same for Float on line 178. The agent had to rewrite using `String.format` after the failure.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A note that Scala's f-interpolator format specifiers must be compile-time literals, and that dynamic precision/width must use `String.format("%." + n + "f", x)` or `"%.%df".format(n).format(x)`.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Extend the String Formatting table with a row for 'dynamic precision / width' mapping Python `f"{x:.{n}f}"` to Scala `String.format(s"%.${n}f", x)`, and add a caveat that `f""` specifiers must be literal.

diagnoses.label: Implicit conversions feature-warning not surfaced
diagnoses.general_pattern: The collections and functional skills freely use `implicit` conversions (e.g. `implicit def fromString`) without noting that Scala 2.13 emits feature warnings unless `import scala.language.implicitConversions` is added or `-language:implicitConversions` is set. Agents translating Python union types via implicit lifts hit these warnings.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Compile output: '4 warnings ... implicit conversion method fromString should be enabled by making the implicit value scala.language.implicitConversions visible.' The agent had to add `import scala.language.implicitConversions` after the fact.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Guidance that any use of `implicit def ...: T` conversion requires the language import (or compiler flag) in Scala 2.13, and that implicit conversions should be used sparingly for union-type ergonomics.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a short note in the type-class / implicit conversion sections stating the required `import scala.language.implicitConversions` for Scala 2.13, and recommend preferring explicit constructors over implicit conversions when translating Python union types.

diagnoses.label: Missing finance-domain guidance for volatility horizon scaling
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill only covers generic Excel mechanics (formulas, formatting, recalc) and provides no domain guidance for financial risk calculations. When a task requires computing a value-at-risk / shock exposure from a periodic volatility, the agent must decide whether to apply a horizon scaling factor (e.g., √n) or use the periodic volatility directly. Without explicit guidance or a validation step, the agent silently over-scales the exposure by an extra √n factor, producing values that are a consistent multiple of the expected answer.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: All row-13 exposures and row-24 RaR values are wrong by the same ratio (~1.7267×), e.g. Belarus risk expected 593.35 vs got 1024.59, Uzbekistan expected 4375.43 vs got 7555.50. The agent's own summary states it used '= reserves × Z × σ_3m × √3 / 100', i.e. it multiplied the already-3-month volatility by √3 again. The skill provided no check or convention for horizon scaling of a period volatility.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A validation/sanity step reminding the agent that a k-period volatility already covers a k-period horizon and should not be multiplied again by √k, and to cross-check exposure magnitudes against an order-of-magnitude expectation before finalizing.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add finance-model guidance (or a dedicated section) noting that when a volatility is already computed over the target horizon, the shock formula is simply value × Z × σ (no extra √n); scaling by √n applies only when converting a shorter-period volatility to a longer horizon. Include a self-check: compare shock/value ratio to Z·σ before saving.

diagnoses.label: No self-verification checklist for numeric outputs against task hints
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill's verification guidance is limited to formula-error detection via recalc.py (#REF!, #DIV/0!, etc.). It does not instruct the agent to sanity-check the numeric results themselves against explicit task hints (e.g., 'near-term valuation swing') or expected magnitudes. As a result, systematically biased numbers pass all checks because no formula error is raised.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Verifier reports 2 failed numeric tests (Step 2 and Step 3) while recalc.py-based checks all passed ('test_no_errors_or_macros PASSED', '1 pre-existing #N/A' dismissed). The agent's final summary confidently reports the wrong numbers because its only 'verification' was the formula-error scan prescribed by the skill.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A post-computation numeric review step: interpret hints in the prompt, reason about expected magnitude/direction of key outputs, and reconcile any conflict before declaring success.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Extend the Formula Verification Checklist with a 'numeric plausibility review' item: after recalc succeeds, re-derive one or two key outputs by hand or with an independent formula, and compare against qualitative hints in the task before finalizing.

package_assessment.rationale: The failing tests stem from a systematic modeling error (double-application of √n horizon scaling to a 3-month volatility) rather than any Excel/tooling failure: recalc.py reports zero new errors and formulas populate correctly. The provided xlsx skill is purely mechanical and offers no financial-modeling conventions or numeric self-check guidance, so a reusable improvement in the skill (horizon-scaling convention plus a numeric plausibility check) is directly relevant.

diagnoses.label: Missing guidance on multi-model ensembling / picker selection to hit both P and S thresholds
diagnoses.general_pattern: The picker-selection skill describes tradeoffs among STA/LTA, template matching, and deep learning at a high level, but gives no concrete guidance for choosing among the several pretrained deep-learning pickers available in SeisBench (PhaseNet vs EQTransformer vs Skynet vs PickBlue, different `from_pretrained` weights) or for combining/ensembling them when a single model gives asymmetric P vs S performance. The agent picked one PhaseNet weight (`scedc`) and tuned only thresholds, achieving strong P F1 (0.77) but S F1 just below threshold (0.59), with no prompt to try alternative weights, ensemble multiple models, or use an S-specific model.

Agent used only `sbm.PhaseNet.from_pretrained('scedc')` and adjusted P/S thresholds; trajectory shows a stub `models = []` loop that was never populated with alternates. Skill lists many pretrained weights and multiple picking models but offers no selection heuristic.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Decision procedure for choosing/combining pretrained weights and models based on data characteristics (network, sampling rate, magnitude range) and for validating that both P and S recall are adequate, including trying multiple weights or ensembling picks when one phase underperforms.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add explicit guidance that (a) different pretrained weights are trained on different networks and can differ substantially in P vs S performance, (b) when metrics are asymmetric across phases, try alternative weights (e.g., `stead`, `instance`, `ethz`, `original`) or a second architecture (EQTransformer) and either pick the best per phase or ensemble/union picks with per-phase thresholds, and (c) validate on any available labels or held-out sanity checks before committing.

diagnoses.label: No preprocessing recipe for deep-learning pickers (filtering, detrending, resampling, component handling)
diagnoses.general_pattern: Neither the seisbench-model-api skill nor the picker-selection skill specifies concrete preprocessing steps that materially affect pick quality: detrend/demean/taper, bandpass filtering appropriate for local earthquakes, matching the model's expected sampling rate (`model.sampling_rate`), and correct handling of missing components (zero-padded channels). The best-practices section only warns about tiny-amplitude scaling. The agent scaled amplitudes and fixed the zero-column mapping only after noticing files with no picks, and never applied bandpass filtering in the final run, which likely contributed to lower S-wave recall/precision.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document a standard preprocessing pipeline for SeisBench picking (component selection, detrend, taper, bandpass appropriate to local vs regional events, resampling to `model.sampling_rate`, amplitude rescaling for tiny values) and warn that zero-padded channels must be dropped rather than passed as data, since they distort normalization and can suppress S-wave detections.

diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add explicit tuning guidance: expose that `classify` accepts per-phase thresholds, describe the precision/recall tradeoff, recommend lower thresholds for S than P for local events, and suggest sweeping thresholds against any available ground truth or sanity heuristics when the metric is F1 with a tolerance.

diagnoses.label: Missing unit-scale reconciliation guidance for cross-source economic data
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a workflow links data from multiple external sources (e.g., PWT capital stock in millions of 2017 US$ and IMF WEO GDP in billions of national currency), the skill provides no requirement to verify and reconcile units/base-year/currency before using them together in a production function. This lets the model compute Y* = exp(LnZ)*K^α on mismatched scales, producing results off by orders of magnitude while all formulas pass an error check.

diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A sanity-check step that (a) records the units/currency/base-year of every linked series, (b) converts them to a common basis before combining, and (c) validates output magnitudes against expected economic scales rather than only formula-error absence.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add explicit guidance in the xlsx skill for financial/economic models to (1) document units in headers and in a source note for every linked series, (2) require an explicit unit/currency/base-year reconciliation step before combining series across sheets, and (3) include a magnitude/plausibility check on final outputs in addition to the existing zero-formula-errors check.
diagnoses.target_section: Financial models > Formula Construction Rules (extend with a 'Unit and Scale Reconciliation' subsection) and 'Formula Verification Checklist' (add magnitude/plausibility check)

diagnoses.label: Opening detection over-extends into teaching content
diagnoses.general_pattern: The silence-detector uses a fixed baseline from the first N seconds and a smoothing/threshold approach that can overshoot the true opening boundary when opening noise energy is close to early-content energy. There is no guidance to validate or refine the detected opening boundary (e.g., cross-check with a secondary signal, use a shorter/adaptive initial window, or apply a hysteresis around the transition), so a single over-long opening segment is accepted as-is and dominates precision.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: silence-detector reported initial silence of 221s (3.68 min) out of a 10-minute video, and this single segment was accepted without any refinement or sanity check. Verifier failed test_segment_detection_precision at 50% (6/12 detections correct) while recall passed, indicating detected segments (including the very long opening) do not align well with ground-truth boundaries.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: No step in silence-detector or an orchestrating overview to validate the detected opening length against plausible ranges, cross-check the transition with adjacent-window energy contrast, or expose tuning guidance for cases where the opening boundary is ambiguous.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add guidance in silence-detector to (a) sanity-check opening length against total duration and warn/refine when it consumes a large fraction, (b) recommend confirming the transition using a local contrast check around the detected end, and (c) document how to tune threshold_multiplier / initial_window when the opening likely blends into content.

diagnoses.label: Pause detector fragments adjacent low-energy regions
diagnoses.general_pattern: pause-detector emits back-to-back short segments separated by a 1-second gap (e.g., 228–231 and 232–237; 522–524 and 525–527) rather than merging near-adjacent pauses. Because each fragment is scored independently against ground-truth intervals by IoU, small gaps between what is effectively one pause reduce precision. The skill provides no guidance or parameter to merge segments separated by a small gap.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: pauses.json contains pairs like {228–231, 232–237} (1s apart) and {522–524, 525–527} (1s apart). Verifier precision failed at 50% while recall passed, consistent with over-fragmentation producing extra low-IoU detections.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: No merge/coalesce step or documented parameter for combining pauses separated by a short gap before emitting segments; also no guidance in segment-combiner to merge overlapping/adjacent segments across sources.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document and support a minimum-gap merge (e.g., merge_gap seconds) in pause-detector so consecutive low-energy runs separated by a brief blip are unified, and/or add adjacent-segment merging in segment-combiner. Include guidance on choosing merge thresholds relative to min_duration.

diagnoses.label: No end-to-end orchestration and validation guidance
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill package exposes many single-purpose tools but lacks an overarching orchestration document that specifies recommended defaults, sanity checks (e.g., verify opening length, merge near-adjacent pauses, cap total removal), and how to iterate when detection quality is poor. This leaves the agent to run the pipeline linearly and accept first-pass outputs without validating detection quality.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Trajectory shows a straight linear run through extract → energy → silence → pauses → combine → process → report with no intermediate validation, iteration, or parameter tuning. Verifier failed precision only, suggesting a validation/refinement step would have caught the issue.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Missing a top-level 'pipeline usage / validation' guide that instructs: after detection, inspect segment lengths and adjacency, apply merges, and consider re-running with tuned parameters if opening dominates or segments look fragmented.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add an orchestration section (in an existing skill such as report-generator or segment-combiner) describing recommended pipeline order, sanity thresholds, and iterative tuning cues based on intermediate outputs before finalizing the report.

package_assessment.rationale: The pipeline ran without executor or infrastructure errors; all tools succeeded and outputs were well-formed. The verifier failure is specifically about detection precision, driven by (1) an over-long opening from silence-detector and (2) fragmented adjacent pauses from pause-detector—both are behaviors governed by guidance and defaults inside the skill docs, hence skill-controllable.
